break.definition: To separate into pieces or damage.
examples: He breaks a dish by accident sometimes.
She broke her leg while skiing.
The vase has broken into pieces.

choose.definition: To select or pick from options.
examples: She chooses her clothes carefully.
He chose the blue shirt for the interview.
They have chosen a new leader.

draw.definition: To produce a picture using a pen or pencil.
examples: He draws portraits in his free time.
She drew a beautiful flower on paper.
He has drawn a detailed map.

drive.definition: To operate and control a vehicle.
examples: He drives to work every morning.
She drove to the beach last Sunday.
They have driven across the country.

fall.definition: To move downward quickly by force of gravity.
examples: Leaves fall from trees in autumn.
He fell off his bike yesterday.
The snow has fallen all night.

fly.definition: To move through the air with wings or aircraft.
examples: The bird flies over the trees.
They flew to Paris last month.
The pilot has flown this route many times.

forget.definition: To fail to remember or recall.
examples: He forgets his password frequently.
She forgot her umbrella on the bus.
I have forgotten my umbrella.
She gets good grades in school.
He got a new job last month.
They have gotten many presents.

give.definition: To present or bestow something to someone.
examples: She gives flowers to her mother.
He gave me a useful advice yesterday.
They have given us a warm welcome.

grow.definition: To increase in size or develop.
examples: The plant grows quickly in sunlight.
He grew two inches over the summer.
The city has grown significantly.

hide.definition: To put or keep out of sight.
examples: The cat hides under the bed during storms.
He hid the money in a safe box.
She has hidden the surprise present.

know.definition: To be aware of or familiar with.
examples: He knows the answer to every question.
She knew him when they were kids.
I have known her for ten years.

ride.definition: To sit on and control a horse or bike.
examples: She rides her bike to work.
He rode a horse across the field.
They have ridden camels in Egypt.

speak.definition: To express thoughts aloud in words.
examples: She speaks three languages fluently.
He spoke at the conference yesterday.
We have spoken about this issue.
A thief steals valuable items.
Someone stole his bicycle yesterday.
The jewels have been stolen.

take.definition: To lay hold of, receive, or transport.
examples: He takes medicine after meals.
She took a photo of the sunset.
They have taken many photos.
He throws the ball to his dog.
She threw the paper into the trash.
He has thrown away old papers.
He wakes up early every morning.
She woke up at six today.
They have woken up refreshed.

wear.definition: To have clothes or accessories on body.
examples: She wears glasses for reading.
He wore a black suit to the wedding.
The coat has been worn out.

write.definition: To form letters or words on a surface.
examples: She writes articles for a magazine.
He wrote a long letter yesterday.
I have written three chapters so far.

awake.definition: To stop sleeping or cause to wake.
examples: He awakes at sunrise every morning.
The thunder awoke the sleeping child.
She has awoken from her long sleep.

blow.definition: To emit current of air or wind.
examples: A cold wind blows from the north.
She blew out the candles on her cake.
The strong gale has blown down trees.

freeze.definition: To turn into ice or harden with cold.
examples: Water freezes at zero degrees Celsius.
The lake froze over last winter.
The ice cream has frozen hard.
He mistakes kindness for weakness.
She mistook him for her brother.
I have mistaken the date of meeting.
The sun rises in the east.
Prices rose sharply last month.
The river level has risen by two feet.

shake.definition: To vibrate or move back and forth.
examples: He shakes hands when meeting people.
She shook the bottle before drinking.
An earthquake has shaken the city.

swear.definition: To state solemnly or use profanity.
examples: He swears to tell the truth.
She swore an oath in the courtroom.
They have sworn to secrecy.

arise.definition: To emerge or come into existence.
examples: New opportunities arise unexpected.
A problem arose during the meeting.
Complications have arisen unexpectedly.

bear.definition: To carry, endure, or give birth to.
examples: She bears the responsibility bravely.
He bore the pain without complaining.
She has borne three children.

forbid.definition: To prohibit or order not to do.
examples: Law forbids driving without license.
My doctor forbade me to drink coffee.
Entry has been forbidden to public.

forgive.definition: To pardon or stop feeling anger.
examples: She forgives minor mistakes easily.
He forgave his friend after apology.
We have forgiven their shortcomings.
He forsakes worldly ambitions.
She forsook her career for family.
They have forsaken their old habits.

outgrow.definition: To grow too large for something.
examples: The child outgrows clothes quickly.
He outgrew his fear of dark.
She has outgrown her childhood toys.

overtake.definition: To catch up with and pass.
examples: A fast car overtakes slow truck.
She overtook her rival near finish line.
Inflation has overtaken wage growth.

overthrow.definition: To depose or remove from power.
examples: Rebels overthrow oppressive regime.
The army overthrew government in coup.
Dictators have been overthrown.
The experiment proves the hypothesis.
The theory proved correct in lab.
His loyalty has been proven.

saw.definition: To cut wood with a saw tool.
examples: The carpenter saws wooden planks.
He sawed log into firewood logs.
The fallen tree has been sawn.

sew.definition: To join or repair with needle/thread.
examples: She sews custom dresses at home.
He sewed button back onto shirt.
The quilt has been sewn by hand.

shave.definition: To cut hair off skin with razor.
examples: He shaves every morning before work.
She shaved her legs for summer.
He has shaved off his beard.
The farmer shears sheep in spring.
They shorn flock in record time.
All sheep have been shorn clean.
Farmers sow seeds in springtime.
She sowed wildflower seeds in field.
Generosity has sown good goodwill.

stride.definition: To walk with long decisive steps.
examples: He strides confidently onto stage.
She strode across room to speak.
He has stridden into the room.

strive.definition: To make great efforts to achieve.
examples: She strives for excellence always.
He strove to overcome his limits.
They have striven for equality.

swell.definition: To expand or increase in size.
examples: An ankle swells after an injury.
Her eye swelled after bee sting.
His ankle has swollen noticeably.

tread.definition: To crush underfoot or walk on.
examples: Protesters tread on unjust laws.
Marchers trod path through snow.
Grass has been trodden down.

withdraw.definition: To remove, take back, or retreat.
examples: He withdraws cash from ATM machine.
Troops withdrew from border town.
She has withdrawn her candidacy.

befall.definition: To happen to or occur to someone.
examples: Tragedy befalls unaware travelers.
Misfortune befell the expedition team.
Great luck has befallen them.
Wind bestrews autumn leaves ground.
Petals bestrewed path before bride.
Flowers have bestrewn the hall.
He browbeats junior staff members.
Lawyer browbeat witness into confession.
Witnesses were browbeaten in court.

hew.definition: To chop or cut with axe.
examples: Lumberjacks hew timber in forest.
He hewed statue from granite block.
Columns were hewn from marble quarry.
Captain overrides automatic controls.
Manager overrode previous decision.
Veto has been overridden by board.

rewrite.definition: To write again or revise text.
examples: Author rewrites draft story chapter.
She rewrote essay to improve flow.
Article has been rewritten cleanly.
Hero slays mythical dragon beast.
David slew Goliath with sling.
Monster has been slain by hero.
Wind strews autumn leaves lawn.
Children strewed toys across room floor.
Papers have been strewn everywhere.
Scientist undertakes complex study.
Company undertook major expansion.
We have undertaken new project.
Weaver weaves tapestry on loom.
She wove colorful carpet pattern.
Stories have been woven into myth.

forswear.definition: To formally renounce or give up.
examples: He forswears alcohol for good.
She forswore violence in protest.
Monks have forsworn luxury items.
His forceful personality overbears dissent.
Evidence overbore defense arguments.
Objections were overborne completely.

smite.definition: To strike down or afflict severely.
examples: Disaster smites the prideful king.
Plague smote ancient empire city.
He was smitten with sudden illness.
